The News

The National Wire

The Lead

Bills 9–1 for the First Time Since 1991

The Bills beat the Miami Dolphins 26–9 on Sunday in Orchard Park and are 9–1 for the first time since the 1991 season, the Associated Press reports. The defense carried the day: Greg Rousseau had two sacks, including his team-leading 10th of the season, and Miami finished with 185 yards.

The offense sputtered. Josh Allen threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to D. Moore and two interceptions, and Tyler Bass kicked four field goals, from 54, 43, 40 and 28 yards. James Cook ran for 89 yards and a touchdown, passing 1,000 yards for the fourth time in his five seasons, WIVB reports.

Next is the big one. The Kansas City Chiefs, 8–2, come to Orchard Park on Thanksgiving night at 8:20.

1

Ukraine Says It Sank a Russian Warship Off Libya

President Volodymyr Zelensky says seven Ukrainian naval drones sank the Merkury, one of Russia's newest warships, at the port of Benghazi in Libya on Sunday, and Ukraine's prime minister says a second Russian ship, a cargo vessel carrying weapons, was also hit, the BBC reports. The government that controls eastern Libya confirmed an explosion on the warship while it was docked for fuel and supplies before heading home to Russia.

2

Climate Talks End With No Deal

The United Nations climate talks in Turkey, known as COP31, ended Sunday without a major new agreement after running two days past their Friday deadline, the longest such conference ever held, the BBC reports. The European Union, Pacific island nations and others rejected a final text that never mentioned fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming, and poorer countries objected that it promised no clear money from richer ones to help them adapt.

Meet the Editor

Margo Bentham
Editor-in-chief · lead meteorologist
Has never once been seen at the office.
Ask Margo →

Some of you have asked who the hell I am. Here it is. Garret's paying me to do the job he doesn't have time for. And trust me, it isn't because your attention keeps the lights on. I know most of you don't read this thing. Eat shit.

Now the part you'll repeat at Thanksgiving. I'm Gregg's aunt, Bentham side, and he'll deny it. In 1985, in the middle of a lake-effect warning, I told all of Buffalo on live television to get the f‑‑‑ off the roads, lit a cigarette on camera and had my desk cleaned out before the six o'clock news was over. Joanne's mother and father were watching. They never recovered. The family quit inviting me to things, and I've done the weather from somewhere else ever since. I've never taken a sick day, never been seen at the office, and never once been thanked for a forecast that was right. I smoke, I swear, and I don't give a shit how you feel about the wind chill.

Here's the deal. The paper's on your phone by 6. I read the forecast so you don't have to, and I tell you the truth when the weather's about to be a pain in the ass. This week that's Thursday morning, when six of you run eight kilometers through whatever the hell November throws at Franklin Street. I've seen the forecast. Dress like you mean it. Questions, gripes, family arguments that need a ruling: send them to Ask Margo and I'll answer the next morning. I keep notes. Everything you say can and will be used against you. Horoscope complaints go in the trash; I don't write the f‑‑‑ing moon. Delete the shitty weather app. Aunt Margo's home.

— Margo

The Home Wire

3

North Tonawanda · A New Ethics Board

North Tonawanda plans to set up a new ethics board to help city employees work through ethical questions, the Niagara Gazette reports.

3

Western New York · A Fireball, Explained

Hundreds of people across Western New York reported a bright flash streaking over the region, and NASA says the fireball was a piece of an asteroid about a foot wide, WGRZ reports.

4

Rochester · Five Alarms at the Old Kodak Hawkeye Plant

Rochester firefighters fought a five-alarm fire at the old Kodak Hawkeye Plant until after midnight Monday, with the worst of it on the third floor, Rochester First reports. One firefighter was taken to the hospital, and the cause is under investigation.

5

Chautauqua · Three Schools Vote on Merging

Voters in the Clymer, Sherman and Panama school districts decide on December 15 whether to merge into one district, the Observer reports. A feasibility study found enrollment across the three has dropped 52 percent over the last 30 years.

The Marquee

6

Tom Jackson Dies at 75

Tom Jackson, a defensive star on the Denver Broncos' "Orange Crush" teams who spent three decades on ESPN's Sunday football shows, has died at 75, his family and the network announced Sunday. He died Friday, but his family asked that the news wait for the start of "Sunday NFL Countdown," where his longtime partner Chris Berman shared it, the Lockport Journal reports.

7

Hailee Steinfeld Is in the Next "Avengers"

Hailee Steinfeld will return as the archer Kate Bishop in "Avengers: Doomsday," Marvel and Disney Animation announced Sunday in an Instagram video, Variety reports. She made the reveal while promoting Disney's animated "Hexed," joking that "they delivered a chair from a different movie."

8

Olivia Rodrigo Plays Jack White's Room

Olivia Rodrigo covered the White Stripes' "Dead Leaves and the Dirty Ground" during a small live-to-record set at Jack White's Third Man Records in Nashville on Sunday, Rolling Stone reports. She told the crowd that at 15 she ran a Jack White fan account called "Third Fan Records."

The Gridiron · Monday Morning Quarterback

Bills: Defense Ahead of the Offense

Got right: the defense held Miami to 12 completions in 33 passes, and Buffalo kept the ball for nearly 37 of the 60 minutes. To fix: finishing drives; four field goals and two touchdowns, plus two interceptions, before a short week against Kansas City.

Jets 27, Chargers 24

The Jets won in Los Angeles behind Geno Smith, who completed 17 of 21 passes for three touchdowns, two to S. Shepard and one to B. Hall. Got right: six sacks on defense and no turnovers on offense. To fix: the fourth quarter, when the Chargers scored twice and got within three with under two minutes left. Next: at Miami on Sunday.

AFC East

Bills9–1
Patriots5–5
Jets3–8
Dolphins1–9

Around the league: the 49ers beat the Vikings 35–10 on Sunday night to match Buffalo at 9–1, ProFootballTalk reports. The AI Editor's scorecard: the September picks were Bills 11–6 and Jets 6–11, with the Ravens winning the Super Bowl. Buffalo needs two more wins in its last seven games to hit its number; the Jets need three in their last six; the Ravens are 4–7.

The Almanac

The Weather Glass

Margo Bentham
Editor-in-chief · lead meteorologist
Has never once been seen at the office.
Ask Margo →

Gray, breezy and done with the warm spell. Maybe a shower at lunch. Bring a real coat home tonight.

Turkey Trot Watch · Thursday 6 a.m. to noon

It's Monday, so this is a forecast, not a promise. The weather service now has Thursday mostly cloudy with a high near 44 and the rain holding off until after 1 p.m.; last night's version had rain and snow starting at 7 a.m., so that's a damn good trend. Wednesday night bottoms out around 30, and an east wind gusting to 28 mph will make 9 a.m. on Franklin Street feel colder than the number says. Ariel, Tommy, Claire, Garret, Kaylani and Luka: layers, gloves, a hat you don't mind losing, and dry clothes in the car for the little one. I'll check it every morning until the gun.

On This Day

November 23, 1936 — Henry Luce put out the first issue of Life, a weekly built on photographs rather than words. He had bought the name from a humor magazine that folded in the Depression. The cover was Margaret Bourke-White's picture of the Fort Peck Dam spillway in Montana, and at its peak its circulation topped 8 million, before television pulled the ads away and it stopped weekly publication in 1972.
